title: Slice-aware elastic batcher to reduce KV fragmentation and GPU memory spikes for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement and validate a 'slice-aware elastic batcher' for streaming chat completions that minimizes KV cache churn and GPU memory fragmentation while preserving tail latency SLOs.

Background: continuous batching for streaming chat presents a tension: aggressive batching raises throughput but increases per-request tail latency and KV cache pressure (large, fragmented KV allocations across sessions). Existing heuristics (session-aware microbatching, watermarks) reduce latency jitter but don't address memory fragmentation on long-lived GPUs when many sessions pin small, sparsely-used KV slots.

Proposal summary: introduce a two-tier formation heuristic: (1) slice reservation per active session: allocate logical KV-slices (configurable 32/64 token windows) mapped to compact GPU slab allocations rather than per-request allocations; (2) elastic batcher that forms micro-slices across sessions with compatible slice-alignment, prioritizing slices that allow contiguous KV placement to reduce fragmentation.

Key properties and decisions:
- Slice granularity: default 64-token slices; configurable by model/profile. Smaller slices reduce memory pressure for short responses but increase batching overhead.
- Affinity scoring: sessions are scored by (estimated remaining tokens, client latency tolerance, cache-hit probability). Batcher prefers mixing high-cache-affinity sessions with low-affinity ones only when slab compaction will not increase fragmentation.
- Slab allocator integration: change from naive per-session allocation to a slab arena that prefers contiguous slice placement; implement lightweight compaction triggers when free-slab ratio drops below threshold.
- KV eviction policy: prefer LRU-with-segmentation (segment by slice age) to avoid evicting recently used prefixes from sessions still streaming.
- Backpressure and fallbacks: when slab saturation threatens SLOs, fallback to prioritized single-request execution (preemptive micro-slices) with temporary KV compression (float16 quantized keys) to avoid OOM.

Implementation artifacts:
- batcher core: new `slice_pool` module + scoring function in continuous-batcher loop.
- slab allocator: `gpu_slab_arena` with compaction counters and hint APIs for batcher.
- telemetry: new metrics (slice_allocation_rate, slab_fragmentation_ratio, kv_eviction_by_reason, slice_compaction_count).

Acceptance criteria:
1) p50 streaming latency <= baseline + 10ms and p95 <= baseline + 30ms under mixed workloads (50/50 short/long sessions).
2) average GPU memory fragmentation ratio reduced by >= 35% in the long-tail test (10k long sessions).
3) no regression in token throughput; throughput change within +/-5% vs baseline.
4) new metrics instrumented and surfaced in console runtime dashboard.

Rollout plan:
- Canary A (internal): run new batcher on runtime-canary-2 in us-west with 5% traffic for 48h.
- Canary B (customer opt-in): invite two mid-market customers with streaming workloads (opt-in) for 1 week.
- Gradual ramp to 25% -> 60% -> full with automatic rollback on memory OOM or p95 spike > 2x.

Open trade-offs and unknowns:
- Slice size tuning: may need model-specific defaults; will run grid search across 16/32/64/128 slices.
- Compaction cost: compaction may itself cause jitter; we plan to do compaction in low-util windows and prioritize soft compaction (move metadata, free contiguous blocks later).
- Interaction with existing KV prefix caching: we need to ensure slice mapping preserves prefix locality; otherwise cache hit rates may drop.

- Spike notebook + microbenchmarks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SliceElastic-bench

- Add compaction timing guard rails and test compaction during 2-4am maintenance window for canary clusters.
